newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Officials bar alcohol in Gaza Strip.
newsitem.headline: Officials bar alcohol in Gaza Strip.

text.p: Palestinian officials have cancelled licenses to sell, buy, drink or manufacture alcoholic beverages in the Gaza Strip, Palestinian sources said on Friday.
Drinking of liquor, prohibited by Islamic law, was strictly forbidden and harshly punished in Gaza during the 1987-94 Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation.
But since Palestinian self-rule began in 1994, alcohol has increasingly appeared in restaurants, nightclubs and other public places.

A Palestinian official said the curbs were directed against the public consumption of alcohol, which offended Gaza's mainly traditional residents. "As long as they drink in homes, indoors, and hurt no one, we will turn a blind eye," he said.

"The Central Committee for Planning and Organisation has decided to refuse to license or renew licenses for any profession of selling, purchasing, using or manufacturing all kinds of liquor," said a resolution passed last week by the overall licensing body and obtained by Reuters on Friday.
The committee also cancelled licenses issued earlier this year by the Gaza municipality under a law dating from 1935, when the Gaza Strip was under British administration.
